div.head: V Atr 16
div.ab: ⁊ sancte Eadwerdes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoran, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eal Englaland on XV kl. Aprilis,
⁊ sancte Eadweardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eal Englaland on XV kl. Aprilis,
⁊ sancte Eadwardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoran þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eal Englaland on XV kl. Apr'.
And sancte Eadwerdes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eal Englaland on XV kalendas Aprilis.
And the authorities have decided that St Edward's festival shall be celebrated throughout England on the 18th of March.
And the council has determined that the Feast of Saint Edward shall be celebrated throughout England on the fifteenth day before the kalends of April.
And the councillors have decreed that St Edward’s festival is to be celebrated over all England on 18 March.
Und des heiligen [König] Eadward [des Märtyrers] Fest haben die Witan entschieden, dass man über ganz England am 18. März feiern soll.
And the witan have decided that the feast of St Edward [the Martyr, king] is to be celebrated throughout all England on 18 March,
div.note: Ethelred’s murdered brother; see No. 1, pp. 230f., No. 236, pp. 915f. This chapter is omitted in VI Ethelred, perhaps because it was not acceptable in the north.
Feast of Saint Edward: October 13. kalends: The first day of the month. In this case, “fifteen days before the kalends of April” refers to March 18.
